resources.string: A lightweight, private web browser for Android TV and Google TV.\n\nSofa has no accounts, no analytics, no ads and no servers of its own. Your history, bookmarks and settings stay on this device. The only connections it makes are to the sites you visit and, if you ask it to, your search engine\'s suggestions and the filter list addresses you choose.

Stronger ad blocking adds EasyList and EasyPrivacy: more ads, trackers and pop-ups blocked. Sofa downloads these two lists from easylist.to, which sees your IP address, and keeps them in memory: about 4 MB more.\n\nYou can change this any time in Settings.
Keep filter lists up to date?

Sofa blocks ads and pop-ups with filter lists, and ad networks change their addresses all the time. Sofa can download the lists that are on again every few days, without cookies, from each list\'s address: GitHub for the built-in ones, easylist.to for EasyList and EasyPrivacy. Those sites see your IP address.\n\nYou can change this any time in Settings.

Video is decoded with the TV\'s hardware where the format allows. Sofa Player shows the streams it plays at full resolution, up to 4K. Video left to the site\'s player goes through Sofa\'s HD window, and 4K TVs upscale it.
Your TV\'s web engine is out of date

Sofa shows pages with the web engine that comes with your TV (Android System WebView). This one is quite old. Sofa can\'t update it, but your TV can: check its app store, or the TV maker\'s updates. Older versions may be missing security fixes, and some sites may not work properly. You can keep browsing in the meantime.

Open the app store on your TV and look for \"Android System WebView\", then choose Update. If your TV has no app store, updates come with the TV\'s system updates, so check its settings or the maker\'s website.
